title: Integrated Finance Playbook: Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement & Revenue Recognition (2027 Update)
author: Priya Malhotra
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's operational guidance for: budgeting and forecasting, contracts and legal intake, procurement procedures, and revenue recognition & billing policies. It is intended for Finance, Legal, Purchasing, and relevant engineering/product stakeholders involved in planning, contracting, and invoicing.

Scope

- Applies to all business units and product lines (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private)
- Covers annual and quarterly budgeting cadence, contract intake and approval, procurement thresholds and preferred vendor process, and rev-rec billing rules for subscription and usage-based products

1) Budgeting & Forecasting

Summary
- Annual planning is owned by Finance with inputs from Product, Sales, Engineering, and GTM. Rolling quarterly forecasts align to ARR/usage, COGS (inference cost), and headcount.

Calendar & Key Deliverables
1. August - November: Annual planning cycle (target budget submitted by business units by Nov 15)
2. Monthly: Rolling forecast update (by 7th business day)
3. Quarterly: Re-forecast for mid-quarter adjustments (owner: FP&A)

Forecasting Inputs & Assumptions
- Revenue drivers: new customer bookings, expansion bookings, usage growth rate (tokens/embedding units), churn assumptions
- Cost drivers: GPU inference hours, storage, egress, third-party services, SRE/on-call overtime, software license renewals
- Headcount plans by role and hire timeline

Approval Matrix (Budget vs. Spend)
| Item | < $50k | $50k–$250k | > $250k |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Operational spend (non-headcount) | Manager | Finance Director | CFO approval + Legal (if contract) |
| Capital / Multi-year commitments | Finance Director | CFO | CEO + Board (if > $1M) |

2) Contracts & Legal Intake Process

Objectives
- Ensure commercial terms, IP, data residency, and security obligations are reviewed and approved; minimize legal risk and ensure consistent revenue recognition treatment.

Contract Intake Steps (standard SLA: 5 business days initial review)
1. Requestor submits contract via Legal intake form (link included in Related Pages).
2. Legal triages: category (standard SaaS, enterprise with DPA, reseller, partner, vendor) and risk bucket (low/medium/high).
3. For standard SaaS agreements, use approved playbook template and routing (no redlines for standard terms).
4. For enterprise/custom agreements: Legal assigns counsel and prepares negotiation plan. Finance provides billing and revenue recognition guidance.
5. Sign-off: Legal + Finance sign for revenue terms; Security signs for data residency/controls where required; Executive approval required for discounts > 40% or multi-year concessions.

Contract Metadata (to capture at intake)
- Contract type, start/end dates, billing frequency, termination terms, total value, renewals, data residency, confidentiality class, required SLOs, redline history.

3) Procurement Procedures

Procurement Thresholds & Approvals
- Spot purchase < $5k: Requestor may approve with departmental budget owner.
- $5k–$50k: Department head approval + Purchasing notification.
- $50k–$250k: Finance Director approval + standard PO and vendor onboarding checklist.
- > $250k: CFO approval, legal review, vendor risk assessment, and (for multi-year or strategic deals) procurement committee review.

Preferred Vendor Onboarding Checklist
1. Vendor W-9 / tax docs
2. Completed security questionnaire (If storing/processing customer data)
3. Approved contract or SOW (with legal sign-off)
4. Banking details + PO terms
5. Insurance certificates if required

Procurement Workflow (numbered)
1. Requestor raises purchase request in procurement system with business justification and budget code.
2. Purchasing validates vendor onboarding status; if not onboarded, trigger onboarding checklist.
3. PO is generated once approvals are complete; vendor receives PO and invoice routing instructions.
4. Finance validates invoice against PO and receipts, applies appropriate GL codes, and processes payment per payment terms.

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies

Principles
- Revenue recognition follows ASC 606 principles: identify contract, performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate, and recognize when performance obligations are satisfied.
- Distinguish between subscription (time-based) and usage (consumption-based) revenue. One-time professional services follow separate recognition rules tied to deliverables.

Common Scenarios
- Hosted API subscriptions (monthly/annual): Recognize ratably over the subscription term. If upfront discounts or credits are present, amortize the discount over the term.
- Usage-based billing (tokens/embeddings): Invoice monthly for measured usage; recognize revenue in the period the usage occurs. For significant estimation (late usage metering), apply estimate and true-up in subsequent month.
- On-prem / Private deployments with multi-element (license + support + deployment): Allocate transaction price across elements based on standalone selling prices; recognize license revenue per contract terms (often at delivery) and support ratably.

Billing Controls and Invoice Rules
- Invoices must reference contract ID and PO (when applicable).
- Billing cadence: monthly in arrears for usage; monthly/annual in advance for subscriptions per contract terms.
- Dispute SLA: Billing disputes must be raised within 30 days of invoice; Finance investigates within 7 business days.

Deferred Revenue & Journal Entries (examples)
- Subscription annual prepayment: Debit Cash, Credit Deferred Revenue; Recognize Revenue monthly as Deferred Revenue -> Revenue.
- Usage accrual at month end (if invoice issued next month): Accrue Estimated Revenue and reverse upon invoicing.

Key Metrics & Reporting
- Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR), Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR), Net Revenue Retention (NRR), Days Sales Outstanding (DSO), deferred revenue balances.
- Finance maintains a monthly close checklist that includes revenue cutoffs and usage reconciliations.
